transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Hi. Thanks. Um, I guess what made me come in is that... well, after work or class, I’ll sit down with my laptop and just end up eating a whole takeout meal, plus chips, sweets, and whatever other snacks I have in my desk drawer. It ends up being way more food than I ever planned to eat, and honestly, it's a lot more than I’d ever eat if anyone else was around.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. Um, I've never tried to make myself throw up or used laxatives or anything like that. And I'm definitely not exercising for hours to work it off. I mostly just... sit there feeling really full and bad about it, but I don't do anything to try and undo it.
How often do these episodes of eating much more than planned happen, and how long has this been going on?

Well, I was actually trying to figure that out before I came in. When I looked back through my journal and my food delivery charges, I realized these episodes have been happening most weeks since the restructuring started at work. It's usually more than once a week, honestly... so, yeah, it's not just happening here and there.
How many months ago did the restructuring at work start, and has this pattern of overeating episodes been going on since then continuously?
Um, it was about four months ago. That's when the office restructuring happened and all these late-night reporting deadlines started. And yeah, it's been going on pretty continuously since then.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of eating objectively large amounts of food (whole takeout meal plus additional snacks) with a sense of loss of control, occurring more than once weekly for approximately 4 months, temporally linked to a psychosocial stressor (work restructuring/deadlines). Episodes are marked by eating alone/more than when others are present and subsequent feelings of fullness and distress/guilt, consistent with markers of loss-of-control eating. Critically, the patient explicitly denies any compensatory behaviors (no vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise), ruling out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). The clinical picture is most consistent with Binge Eating Disorder, which is coded under ICD-10 as F50.8 (Other specified eating disorder) since ICD-10 lacks a distinct BED code.

confirmed_symptoms: Eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period (whole takeout meal plus chips, sweets, and other snacks)
Eating more than would be eaten if others were present (implying eating alone due to embarrassment)
Feeling uncomfortably full and feeling bad/distressed after eating
Denies laxative or other medication misuse

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Episodes occurring more than once per week, continuously for approximately 4 months since onset of work restructuring stressor.
additional_requirements: Frequency of binge episodes exceeds once weekly
